name: PRODUCTION
label: Month 6 · Docker, deploy, streaming, cost
goal: Get it on the internet with a public URL. Ship the mobile app.

weeks.title: Docker and reproducible packaging
weeks.why: 'It works on my machine' ends the conversation in a system design round. Containerising an ML-adjacent app has real gotchas — model weights, slow builds, huge images — that plain web apps do not have.

tasks.t: Dockerfile fundamentals: layers, caching, .dockerignore, why your image is 4GB
Multi-stage builds with uv. Get the API image under 500MB.
Model weights: bake into the image vs mount vs download at boot. Understand the cold-start tradeoff.
docker compose: api + postgres/pgvector + redis, with healthchecks and depends_on conditions
Config and secrets: env vars, .env, never bake a key into a layer (it stays in history even if deleted)
Make `docker compose up` bring the entire stack to life from a fresh clone. Test it by actually cloning fresh.

resources.label: uv in Docker — official integration guide

weeks.deliverable: A fresh clone + `docker compose up` = the full stack running. No manual steps.
weeks.checkpoint: Time a rebuild after a one-line code change. If it is over 30 seconds, your layer order is wrong.

weeks.title: Deploy it for real (on free tiers)
weeks.why: A live URL is worth more than three more repos. 'Deployed with a live demo' is in the target JD. Do it on free infrastructure, and learn the AWS vocabulary in parallel because JDs ask for it.

tasks.t: Pick a free host: HuggingFace Spaces (free, you know HF), Render, Fly.io, or Railway. Deploy the FastAPI backend.
Managed Postgres free tier for pgvector: Supabase or Neon. Migrate your vector store to it.
uvicorn workers, graceful shutdown, healthcheck endpoint, /readyz vs /healthz
AWS vocabulary for interviews (free tier hands-on where possible): EC2, ECS/Fargate, Lambda, S3, ALB, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch. Know what each is FOR.
Cold starts, keeping a free instance warm, and the honest tradeoffs of serverless for LLM apps
Put the live URL in your README and on your resume

resources.label: HuggingFace Spaces — free hosting for demos (Docker SDK supported)
freeCodeCamp — AWS Cloud Practitioner full course (free, enough for JD vocabulary)
Fly.io — free allowance and deploy docs

weeks.deliverable: A public URL anyone can hit, backed by managed Postgres+pgvector.
weeks.checkpoint: Send the URL to a friend on mobile data. Does it work? Does it stay up for a week?

weeks.title: Streaming, caching, and cost engineering
weeks.why: This is where your mobile background becomes an actual differentiator. Almost nobody applying for these roles has streamed LLM tokens into a native app and dealt with reconnects on a flaky mobile network.

tasks.t: SSE consumption in React Native: fetch streaming limits, react-native-sse, or WebSocket fallback. Handle backgrounding and reconnect.
Perceived latency: time-to-first-token beats total time. Optimise TTFT specifically and measure it.
Provider prompt caching — restructure prompts so the static prefix is cacheable. Measure the cost drop.
Semantic caching with an embedding threshold. Measure hit rate AND false-hit rate (a wrong cache hit is worse than a miss).
Model routing: cheap model for easy queries, expensive for hard. Build the classifier, measure cost saved vs quality lost.
Rate limiting, request queues, timeouts, and graceful degradation when the provider is down

DESIGN VOCABULARY: while it's fresh, write down what you just built as design language — cache layers, rate limiting, backpressure, graceful degradation, TTFT. You now have real answers to 'how would you scale this'; name them before you forget.

resources.label: Chip Huyen — AI engineering patterns and cost optimisation

weeks.deliverable: A measured cost/latency table: before and after caching + routing. Another number for the resume.
weeks.checkpoint: What is your cache hit rate, and what is your FALSE hit rate? If you only know the first, you have a quality bug waiting.

weeks.title: PROJECT A SHIP — the AI mobile app
weeks.why: This is your unfair advantage, and the reason you will beat ML-bootcamp candidates. They cannot build this. A React Native app streaming from your own RAG backend, deployed, with a demo video, is a portfolio nobody else in your bracket has.

tasks.t: RN front end: chat UI, token streaming, citations rendered from retrieved chunks, loading and error states
Offline and flaky-network handling — this is the mobile-specific engineering nobody else demos
Auth, per-user data isolation, and per-user spend caps
Wire the deployed backend. End-to-end on a real device over mobile data.
Record a 2-minute demo video. Put it at the top of the README and on LinkedIn.
README written for a hiring manager: what it does, architecture diagram, metrics table, live link, demo video

resources.label: Expo EAS Build — ship a real installable build free
How to write a README that gets you hired

weeks.deliverable: PROJECT A: a deployed AI mobile app with a live backend and a 2-minute demo video.
weeks.checkpoint: Hand your phone to someone who does not code. Can they use it without instructions?
